findings.title: Multi-start returns plans above what a wider seed set reaches with the same minimizer on the same objective
findings.claim: On the 80-cell grid (8 price x 5 weather x single/two-zone, DHW off, 24 h), production's _multi_start_minimize result is above the best feasible challenger on its own captured objective by more than 1e-3 relative in 26 cells and by more than 1e-2 in 2 cells (max 5.06e-2). Most of this is reached by C1, the same minimizer with structured seeds added.

evidence.contention_note: fan-out, about 3 seats on the box, load1 15.88; counts and objective ratios are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-maxiter 20 (the production call runs at maxiter 20); on tz=1 winter_typical/winter_cold

findings.metric_definition: gap_rel = (f(prod.x) - min feasible challenger f) / |f(prod.x)|, where f is the captured production objective. A challenger is feasible only if its room band violation is no worse than production's.
findings.phenomenon_property: The candidate set production seeds into L-BFGS-B misses basins that price-ranked bang-bang and constant-level seeds reach. The returned plan is then not the minimum of production's own objective that production's own minimizer can find.
findings.seam_rule: dev/audit/rounds/round10/D0/s1/race.py (each call captured at _multi_start_minimize; the by=c1 column marks the seed-caused gaps)

findings.title: No check pins that a raising weather fetch keeps the previous forecast; the and->or mutant at coordinator.py:6522 survives
findings.claim: Flipping `if state and not self._weather_forecast:` to `or` in HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator._fetch_weather_forecast replaces a 24-row previous forecast with the fabricated 48-row constant trajectory (prior_kept 1 -> 0), and the file's whole non-structural closure plus env_drift --all stays green on that mutant (M08 SURVIVED).
findings.mechanism: tests/features.py 'Weather staleness is surfaced (M2)' covers three cases: a raise with no prior forecast (fabricates), an empty result with a prior forecast (keeps), and a good fetch. It does not cover a raise with a prior forecast. The method's own docstring says the fabricated constant forecast cost +41.9 % realized and may be built only when nothing better exists.

findings.title: get_current_action's 12 per-key length guards are live but no check feeds them a short schedule; M01 and M03 survive
findings.claim: With any optional schedule shorter than power_schedule, flipping `and` to `or` in each of the 12 `if result.X and i < len(result.X)` guards in HeatPumpOptimizer.get_current_action raises IndexError (12 of 12 live). Two sampled flips, at optimizer.py:5541 and 5557, survive the full non-structural closure plus env_drift --all.
findings.mechanism: Every test plan builds schedules of equal length, so the length half of each guard is never exercised. A refactor that drops it would pass the gate and crash the action read if a shorter schedule ever reached it. Whether production can produce a shorter schedule is not shown, hence severity low.

findings.title: Two-zone continuation pays 288 SSE per gradient instead of the fused 97
findings.claim: _optimize_space_only.move_starts runs L-BFGS-B with a callable jac that evaluates float(objective(x)) as f0 plus a scalar fun. Each gradient costs 96 batch rows + 2 scalar horizons = 288 SSE, against 97 for the fused value-and-gradient the main loop uses. Across a 6-cell two-zone no-DHW grid, fusing removes 13.5-31.1% of total solve SSE, or 13.5-29.2% after dropping the largest cell. The flat-price cell removes 29.2%, so the cost does not depend on prices. The iterate path is unchanged: main gradient counts are identical in both arms.

evidence.value: cont sse_per_grad 192 in the jac + 96 in cont_fun per grad (288 total); with fuse 97. winter_two_zone_no_dhw total SSE 62121 -> 53717
evidence.contention_note: Counts are exact and contention-immune. Continuation CPU 314->204 ms (and 5 other cells) was taken at load1 ~20-26 and is provisional.

perturbation.change: --perturb fuse: give the continuation the fused value+gradient (jac=True, x as row 0 of the batch), as _fused_value_and_gradient does
perturbation.expected_direction: cont sse_per_grad 288 -> 97; cont_fun SSE -> 0; total SSE falls 13.5-31%; main grads unchanged

findings.metric_definition: (scalar simulate_step calls + simulate_trajectory_batch rows) per _batch_fd_gradient call, split by phase (main fused / continuation jac / continuation fun)
findings.phenomenon_property: An L-BFGS-B call inside a solve that passes a callable jac rather than the fused jac=True evaluates the objective at each iterate as separate scalar horizons on top of the batched gradient.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: In _optimize_space_only.move_starts, build the continuation's fun with _fused_value_and_gradient(objective_batch, bounds, 1e-4) and jac=True, matching _multi_start_minimize.

findings.title: _gil_yield's sleep(0) does not bound the loop starvation of an in-process solve
findings.claim: On the #511 in-process fallback, the solve runs on an executor thread. During a two-zone solve the event-loop heartbeat's max gap is 87-124 ms and the starvation share is 0.70-0.89. The idle null control in the same session shows 14-21 ms and 0.08-0.17. Removing _gil_yield barely changes the gap, while a real 0.1 ms sleep cuts it to about 30 ms. So the per-evaluation sleep(0) does not act as a GIL handoff.

evidence.value: max gap winter_two_zone_dhw 123.9 ms, shoulder_two_zone 86.6 ms (idle 14.1); realsleep: 29.4 / 32.1 ms
evidence.contention_note: load1 16-28 (saturated box); all values provisional and must be re-taken in a quiet window
evidence.thread_factor: 1.002 (residual after subtracting the deliberate executor thread CPU)

perturbation.change: --perturb realsleep: _gil_yield sleeps 0.1 ms instead of sleep(0)
perturbation.expected_direction: max heartbeat gap falls (measured 124->29 ms, 87->32 ms)

findings.metric_definition: Max gap between 1 ms asyncio heartbeat ticks on a real loop while HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize runs in a ThreadPoolExecutor; starvation share = wall fraction covered by gaps > 5 ms
findings.phenomenon_property: A GIL yield implemented as time.sleep(0) inside the solver thread does not hand the GIL to a waiting event-loop thread.
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Make _gil_yield a real handoff (a sub-ms non-zero sleep, rate-limited), or document that only the process-worker path bounds the hold. Re-measure quiet first.
